chunks: A man asked him and said to him:
I have a mosque at the entrance of my house. Which of the two is better: that I pray in my home and lengthen the salat (prayer), or that I pray with them and make it lighter?
So he, peace be upon him (AS), wrote: "Lead them in salat (prayer), perform the prayer well, and do not make it burdensome."
And indeed ʿAlī, peace be upon him (AS), said:
Regarding two men who disagreed, and one of them said, "I was your Imam," and the other said, "I was your Imam," he said: "Their salat (prayer) is complete."
He said: I said, "Then if one of them says: I was following you, and the other says: I was following you?"
He said: "Then their salat (prayer) is invalid, so they must begin again."

key_terms.أَئْتَمُّ: I follow in prayer behind an Imam
key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: your Imam, the one leading the prayer
key_terms.فَلْيَسْتَأْنِفَا: let them repeat or begin the prayer anew
key_terms.مَسْجِدًا: a mosque, the place where congregational salat (prayer) is held

ai.seo_question: What do these hadith say about leading congregational prayer and mistaken intention between Imam and follower?
ai.summary: These narrations address rulings of congregational salat (prayer). The first prefers leading the people with a well-performed but not burdensome prayer, while the second clarifies how conflicting intentions of imamah and following affect the validity of salat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1121 - A man asked him:
"I have a mosque at the entrance of my house. Which is better—should I pray at home where I can make my prayer longer, or should I lead them (in the mosque) and make it lighter?"
He (as) wrote: "Lead them in prayer and perform it well, but do not make it too heavy (burdensome)”.

1122 - وَ إِنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلَيْنِ اِخْتَلَفَا فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا كُنْتُ إِمَامَكَ وَقَالَ اَلْآخَرُ كُنْتُ إِمَامَكَ قَالَ «صَلاَتُهُمَا تَامَّةٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا كُنْتُ أَئْتَمُّ بِكَ وَقَالَ اَلْآخَرُ كُنْتُ أَئْتَمُّ بِكَ قَالَ «فَصَلاَتُهُمَا فَاسِدَةٌ فَلْيَسْتَأْنِفَا.
Hadith.1122 - Imam Ali (as) said regarding two men who disagreed, with one saying, "I was your Imam (leader in prayer)," and the other saying, "I was your Imam," that "their prayers are valid."
When asked what if one of them said: "I was following you (as the Imam)," and the other also said: "I was following you,"
Imam (as) said: "Then their prayers are invalid, and they must repeat the prayer”.
